reasoning: The failure is a close-range collision with a dynamic obstacle (a large dog's legs in a narrow indoor gap) that resulted in the robot being tipped backward and rolling onto its side. Because the video froze during impact (with a ~1.3–1.4 s timestamp lag relative to the IMU), there is significant uncertainty in the exact kinematics and relative timing of the dog's leg movement versus the robot's approach. To train the policy to robustly avoid close-in dynamic obstacles (dogs/pedestrians) in tight spaces without relying on exact timing, we randomize the obstacle/mover's initial position (`obs_x`, `obs_y`, `ped_start_y`), size (`obs_r`), speed (`ped_speed`), and timing (`ped_t0` to cover the ~1.4 s clock offset and varying reaction windows), along with the robot's approach speed (`observed_speed`) and indoor carpet traction (`friction`).

ranges.why: Covers the close-range re-approach distance (~0.5 m) up to initial encounter distances (~1.5 m) in indoor spaces.
Varies lateral offset around the narrow gap between furniture where the dog's legs were ~0.1–0.15 m off-center.
Spans thin obstacles like a single dog leg (0.08 m) up to the full stance width of a large dog or human legs (0.30 m).
Covers slow indoor creeping (0.25 m/s) up to brisk indoor driving (1.0 m/s) around the estimated 0.45 m/s impact speed.
Account for uncertainty in whether the dog's legs actively shifted/kicked during the frozen video frames (from 0.3 m/s slow shift up to 0.9 m/s sudden step).
Brings the dynamic mover closer or slightly further laterally so the collision zone varies across the robot's path.
Directly addresses the ~1.3–1.4 s video-to-IMU clock offset uncertainty and varies when the dog/mover begins stepping into the path.
Spans typical indoor surfaces from slicker rugs/floors (0.65) to high-grip carpet (1.2) that enables high pitch-up torque on impact.
